title_en: Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. v. Changde Arts and Crafts School — petition for retrial of enforcement ruling

full_text_en:
Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. v. Changde Arts and Crafts School — dispute over refusal to enforce an execution ruling

【Ruling Summary】

1. The voluntary conclusion of a lawful and valid agreement or the selection of an arbitration institution by the parties to resolve their disputes is a prerequisite for the adoption of arbitration as the method of dispute resolution. If the parties have not agreed to submit their disputes to an arbitration institution, the arbitration institution generally has no authority to arbitrate such disputes.

2. Where the parties have agreed in the main contract to refer their disputes to an arbitration institution, the key to determining whether such agreement can apply to a supplementary agreement that does not specify a dispute resolution method lies in whether the main contract and the supplementary agreement are severable. If the main contract and the supplementary agreement are independent and severable from each other, and in the absence of a special stipulation, the dispute resolution method for two completely independent and severable contracts or agreements shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the respective contracts or supplementary agreements. If the supplementary agreement is a supplement to the content of the main contract and must be attached to the main contract and cannot exist independently, then the dispute resolution clause stipulated in the main contract shall also apply to the supplementary agreement.

Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Zhi Shen Zi No. 33

Appellant (Enforcement Applicant): Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 057 East Jianshe Road, Dongtinggong Community, Zhangjiang Town, Taoyuan County, Changde City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Yu Dahua, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Yiyou, Lawyer of Hunan Jingwei Law Firm.

Respondent (Enforcement Respondent): Changde Arts and Crafts School. Domicile: No. 2876 West Binhu Road, Wuling District, Changde City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Yu Peng, Chairman of the Board of the School.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Rongguang, Lawyer of Hunan Changxiang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Gong Zhiyong, Lawyer of Hunan Changxiang Law Firm.

The Appellant, Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court, appealed to this Court. After acceptance, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law for review. This case has now been concluded upon review.

Upon review, this Court finds the following: On July 7, 2011, Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., due to a dispute over unpaid project funds with Changde Arts and Crafts School, applied for arbitration to the Changde Arbitration Commission, requesting a ruling ordering Changde Arts and Crafts School to pay project funds of RMB 2,902,107.5 and interest on the project funds of RMB 156,713.81. Changde Arts and Crafts School filed a counterclaim for arbitration with the Changde Arbitration Commission, requesting that Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. compensate for the losses suffered by Changde Arts and Crafts School due to delays in construction period and poor construction quality. Upon the application of Changde Arts and Crafts School, the Changde Arbitration Commission entrusted Hunan Hongyuan Zhongzhu Engineering Project Management Co., Ltd. to conduct a judicial appraisal of the cost of the electrical and decoration works on the student dormitory building undertaken by Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., in accordance with the settlement standards stipulated in the contract. The appraisal determined the cost of these two parts to be RMB 1,471,605. On January 6, 2012, the Changde Arbitration Commission issued an award (2011) Chang Zhong Cai Zi No. 163, confirming that Changde Arts and Crafts School had paid Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. RMB 2,367,067 in project funds, with the remaining amount unpaid. The award ordered: 1. Changde Arts and Crafts School shall pay Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. the outstanding project funds of RMB 2,442,792.16 within ten days from the date of receipt of the award. 2. Changde Arts and Crafts School shall pay Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. interest on the principal construction project funds for the student dormitory building of Changde Arts and Crafts School (with interest calculated on a base of RMB 971,187.16 from December 4, 2009, to the date of actual payment, at the loan interest rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China for the same period) within ten days from the date of receipt of the award. 3. The request of Changde Arts and Crafts School for Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. to compensate for losses of RMB 600,000 resulting from delays in construction period and substandard quality was not supported.

Changde Arts and Crafts School applied to Changde Intermediate People's Court for non-enforcement of the arbitration award (2011) Chang Zhong Cai Zi No. 163 of the Changde Arbitration Commission, on the following grounds: 1. The arbitration award applied the law incorrectly; 2. The arbitration award had insufficient evidence for the facts found; 3. The arbitration award violated social public interests. On July 19, 2012, the Changde Intermediate People's Court issued an enforcement ruling (2012) Chang Zhi Bu Zi No. 8.

The Changde Intermediate People's Court held that the arbitration tribunal has a certain degree of discretion in finding facts and applying law, and that the parties, having chosen the arbitration route, must bear the corresponding consequences. The review of a request for non-enforcement of an arbitration award by a people's court during enforcement proceedings is different from a retrial of the case. Unless the circumstances set forth in Article 213 of the Civil Procedure Law are present, the court should not easily deny the award. In this case, after receiving the project settlement documents provided by Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., Changde Arts and Crafts School failed to respond within the specified period and also put the project into use before acceptance. Based on this, the arbitration tribunal interpreted the settlement clause of the contract to mean that the failure of Changde Arts and Crafts School to respond within the time limit constituted acceptance of the settlement documents. This finding was not obviously erroneous in terms of fact-finding and application of law. Under the circumstances of this case, the enforcement of the arbitration award did not involve any circumstances that would violate social public interests. The ground of violation of social public interests as a reason for non-enforcement lacked basis. Therefore, the court rejected the application of Changde Arts and Crafts School.

Dissatisfied with the enforcement ruling (2012) Chang Zhi Bu Zi No. 8 of the Changde Intermediate People's Court, Changde Arts and Crafts School appealed to the Hunan High People's Court, requesting supervision and a ruling for non-enforcement of the award, on the following grounds: 1. The agreement and supplementary agreement actually performed by the parties contained no arbitration clause, and the Changde Arbitration Commission erroneously arbitrated the case; 2. The main evidence for the facts found in the arbitration was insufficient. After receiving the project settlement documents from Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., Changde Arts and Crafts School had repeatedly negotiated with Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. on the settlement issues, rather than failing to respond. Therefore, non-enforcement should be ordered; 3. The evidence for the award of interest on project funds was insufficient; 4. The winning bid price for the project was RMB 1,671,814, which did not include electrical and water installation works, decoration works, etc. However, the arbitration determined the cost of electrical and water installation and decoration works to be RMB 1.47 million, which exceeded the scope of the arbitration agreement and should not be enforced.

The Hunan High People's Court held that: "Although the agreement signed on November 30, 2007, did not specify the method of dispute resolution, the contract signed on December 8, 2007, after a bidding process, explicitly stipulated that disputes between the parties should be submitted to the Changde Arbitration Commission. This contract, signed in accordance with administrative regulations and through legal procedures, is a lawful and valid agreement and shall be complied with. The contract clearly specified arbitration jurisdiction, so the Changde Arbitration Commission has jurisdiction over this case. At the same time, the contract also clearly stipulated that pile foundations, interior and exterior decoration, doors and windows, electrical and water installation, and ancillary works were not included in the scope of the contract. Although the supplementary agreement stipulated the cost of electrical and water installation and decoration works, it did not specify the method of dispute resolution. Therefore, the cost of electrical and water installation and decoration works did not fall within the scope of the arbitration agreement. However, the arbitration award made a ruling on this part of the project cost, exceeding the scope of the arbitration. Pursuant to Article 213, Paragraph 2, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in effect at the time, and Article 129 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Execution Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), the court issued an enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 on June 6, 2013, ruling: 1. To revoke the enforcement ruling (2012) Chang Zhi Bu Zi No. 8 of the Changde Intermediate People's Court; 2. To refuse enforcement of the arbitration award (2011) Chang Zhong Cai Zi No. 163 of the Changde Arbitration Commission."

Additional facts found: On November 30, 2007, Changde Arts and Crafts School and Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. signed the "Contract for the Construction and Contracting of the Student Dormitory Building of Changde Arts and Crafts School," in which the parties agreed: The project owner is Changde Arts and Crafts School, and the project contractor is Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. Changde Arts and Crafts School planned to build a student dormitory building with a floor area of 4,100 m². After inspection and verification of Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., Changde Arts and Crafts School agreed to award the contract to Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. In the "1. Project Overview" section, the contracting method was stipulated: (1) Within the scope of the contract for Party B (the contractor) were: turnkey construction according to drawings, changing the cast-in-place slab of the west dormitory building to hollow precast slab, changing all terrazzo floors in both ends of the building to ordinary qualified floor tiles (stairs remain terrazzo), fire protection responsible only for material and labor costs, within 1 meter outside the outer wall of the building. Part of the ±0 elevation increase. (2) Not within the scope of the contract for Party B were: weak current, air conditioning, electric fans, pile foundations; expenses other than material costs for fire protection were the responsibility of Party A. Additional works, in addition to those already included in the budget, included: electrical and water works included, foundations included, weak current wiring and labor costs included, doors M1 and M5 included, first floor floor treatment done according to the standard of floors 2 to 6 included. Works not budgeted for or beyond the design drawings were to be settled according to the 1999 quota and fee standards and the spirit of various price adjustment documents at the time. In the "10. Miscellaneous" section, it was agreed: Matters not covered in this contract may be supplemented through negotiation between the parties, by signing supplementary agreements as attachments, which shall have the same effect as this contract. On December 28, 2007, Changde Arts and Crafts School and Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. signed the "Construction Contract for Construction Projects" (GF-1999-0201), which stipulated the scope of the contract: main civil works. Note: pile foundations, interior and exterior decoration, doors and windows, electrical and water installation, and ancillary works were not within the scope of the contract. In "Part III Special Terms 37. Disputes," it was agreed: Disputes arising during the performance of this contract shall be resolved through negotiation between the parties; if negotiation fails, they shall be submitted to the Changde Arbitration Commission for arbitration. On March 20, 2008, Changde Arts and Crafts School and Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. signed the "Supplementary Agreement to the Contract for the Construction and Contracting of the Student Dormitory Building of Changde Arts and Crafts School," which stated: Party A plans to build a new school dormitory building with a floor area of 4,526 square meters. Through consultation, the parties had signed a contract on December 28, 2007 (contract text GF-1999-0201). In order to perfect the terms and further protect the lawful rights and interests of both parties, the following supplementary agreement is signed for matters not covered and new issues that may arise, to be observed by both parties. The supplementary agreement: 1. The first budget document prepared by Engineer Huang Sheng entrusted by Party A is the basis for the signing of the contract (i.e., the budget is reduced by 15% as the basis for awarding the contract; electrical and water works were not included in the budget but are to be undertaken by Party B). The budget for the main part of the project prepared by Engineer Huang, entrusted solely for bidding purposes by Party B, is only for bidding. When final settlement is made, only the first budget document shall prevail. 2. For energy-saving and other projects added in this project, the contract pricing shall be based on the same budget preparation, with a reduction of 15% from the national standard. 3. The details of the project shall be performed in accordance with the "Contract for the Construction and Contracting of the Student Dormitory Building of Changde Arts and Crafts School" signed by both parties on November 30, 2007. The last page of that contract contains the word "Original." 4. Matters not covered may still be further supplemented by additional supplementary agreements signed after negotiation, and such supplementary agreements shall have the same effect as the previous agreements, and the supplementary terms shall be the final basis for performance.

The Appellant, Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court, appealed to this Court, primarily on the following grounds: 1. The enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court exceeded its authority and illegally accepted the case. The grounds for Changde Arts and Crafts School's application to the Changde Intermediate People's Court for non-enforcement of the arbitration award differed from the grounds for its appeal to the Hunan High People's Court against the ruling rejecting the non-enforcement application; the earlier application did not involve the issue of arbitration jurisdiction. 2. The enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court was not legally served with legal documents, and it did not comply with the provision in the "Provisions of the Hunan High People's Court on Implementation Hearings" that, for a ruling refusing enforcement of an arbitration award made by an arbitration institution, a hearing must be held. 3. The enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court did not evaluate the enforcement ruling (2012) Chang Zhi Bu Zi No. 8 of the Changde Intermediate People's Court, and there was no evidence proving that the enforcement ruling (2012) Chang Zhi Bu Zi No. 8 was erroneous. It directly revoked that ruling and ruled to refuse enforcement of the arbitration award (2011) Chang Zhong Cai Zi No. 163 of the Changde Arbitration Commission, which exceeded the scope of review. Moreover, Changde Arts and Crafts School did not apply for revocation of the arbitration award on the ground that the matters adjudicated exceeded the scope of the arbitration agreement. 4. The enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court had unclear findings of fact. First, the ruling stated that the arbitration award exceeded the contract. In the bidding contract, electrical and water works and decoration works were not included; the supplementary agreement also determined that they were not to be calculated together with the main body. Moreover, the supplementary agreement stipulated the cost of electrical and water installation and decoration works but did not specify the method of dispute resolution. The arbitration award itself noted that the cost of this part was invalid due to lack of bidding, but the award made a ruling on this part of the project cost, which exceeded the arbitration scope. This was inconsistent with the dispute resolution provisions in Article 10, Section 37.1 of the "Construction Contract for Construction Projects" (GF-1999-0201) signed by both parties, the provisions in Articles 8 and 10 of the "Contract for the Construction and Contracting of the Student Dormitory Building of Changde Arts and Crafts School," and the provisions in Article 3 of the "Supplementary Agreement to the Contract for the Construction and Contracting of the Student Dormitory Building of Changde Arts and Crafts School." Second, the dispute resolution method actually chosen by the parties was arbitration. In the arbitration hearing records, both parties explicitly agreed to arbitration jurisdiction. During the arbitration, Changde Arts and Crafts School applied for a judicial appraisal of the project cost for the part covered by the supplementary agreement, paid the appraisal fee, and the arbitration commission made its award based on the appraisal conclusion.

Upon review, this Court holds:

1. Regarding whether the additional grounds for appeal should be reviewed. In the grounds for appeal submitted by Changde Arts and Crafts School to the Hunan High People's Court, it added the content that "the agreement and supplementary agreement actually performed by the parties contained no arbitration clause." Since the requests made by Changde Arts and Crafts School to both the Changde Intermediate People's Court and the Hunan High People's Court were both for non-enforcement of the arbitration award, its substantive request did not change. Therefore, it was not improper for the Hunan High People's Court to review the request based on the specific grounds for appeal (including the newly added grounds).

2. Regarding the appellant's claim that no hearing was held and that legal documents were not served in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 12 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Publicity of Enforcement Work of the People's Courts," a people's court shall generally conduct a public hearing for review of major enforcement matters such as objections by a third party, applications for non-enforcement, and changes or additions of enforcement respondents. If the case is simple, the facts are clear, and a hearing is unnecessary, the people's court may directly conduct the review. Therefore, the Hunan High People's Court had the discretion to decide whether to hold a hearing based on the circumstances of the case. Legal documents issued by a people's court must be served in accordance with the law. In this case, the appellant, Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the enforcement ruling (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court, appealed to this Court, indicating that it was aware of the content of that ruling and submitted the text of that ruling to this Court. However, this does not relieve the Hunan High People's Court of its obligation to serve the documents in accordance with the law.

3. Regarding whether the review by the Hunan High People's Court exceeded the scope of the grounds on which Changde Arts and Crafts School applied for non-enforcement of the arbitration award. Pursuant to Article 213, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in effect at the time, if the respondent provides evidence proving that the arbitration award falls under one of the six circumstances stipulated in this paragraph, the people's court, after having it examined and verified by a collegial panel, shall rule to refuse enforcement. Therefore, it was not improper for the Hunan High People's Court, in reviewing the application of Changde Arts and Crafts School to the court for non-enforcement of the arbitration award, to determine whether the grounds for non-enforcement of the arbitration award were established in accordance with the above provisions.

4. Regarding the issue of whether the arbitral institution may conduct arbitration on both the main contract and the supplementary agreement when the main contract stipulates arbitration as the dispute resolution method but the supplementary agreement does not specify a dispute resolution method. The Court holds that the premise for adopting arbitration to resolve disputes is that the parties voluntarily reach a lawful and valid agreement or arbitration clause to select an arbitral institution to settle their disputes. If the parties have not agreed that their disputes shall be resolved by an arbitral institution, then, under normal circumstances, the arbitral institution has no authority to arbitrate such disputes. However, in cases where there are both a main contract and a supplementary agreement, and the parties have agreed in the main contract that their disputes shall be resolved by an arbitral institution, the key to determining whether this agreement applies to the supplementary agreement, which does not stipulate a dispute resolution method, lies in whether the main contract and the supplementary agreement are severable. If the main contract and the supplementary agreement are independent and severable from each other, then, in the absence of a special agreement, the dispute resolution method for two completely independent and severable contracts or agreements shall be handled in accordance with the contract or supplementary agreement. If the supplementary agreement is intended to supplement the content of the main contract, must be attached to the main contract, and cannot exist independently from the main contract, then the dispute resolution clause agreed upon in the main contract also applies to the supplementary agreement. In this case, the contract signed by the parties on December 28, 2007, after the public tender, expressly provides that any dispute between the parties shall be under the jurisdiction of the Changde Arbitration Commission. Therefore, the Changde Arbitration Commission has jurisdiction over this case. Subsequently, the supplementary agreement signed by the parties on March 20, 2008, expressly states that the parties had signed a contract on December 28, 2007, and that this supplementary agreement was signed to improve the clauses, supplement matters not covered, and address new issues that might arise, and it expressly provides that "the supplementary agreement signed shall have the same effect as the previously signed agreement." It can be seen from this that the dispute resolution clause agreed in the main contract, which provides that disputes shall be submitted to the Changde Arbitration Commission for arbitration, shall also apply to the supplementary agreement. Furthermore, according to the law, if a party has an objection to the validity of the arbitration agreement, it shall be raised before the first hearing of the arbitral tribunal. In this case, after Hunan Huaxia Construction Co., Ltd. applied for arbitration to the Changde Arbitration Commission, Changde Arts and Crafts School did not raise an objection to the validity of the arbitration agreement before the first hearing of the arbitral tribunal. Instead, it submitted a counterclaim for arbitration to the Changde Arbitration Commission and applied to the Changde Arbitration Commission to entrust a judicial appraisal of the project cost of the hydropower and decoration works in accordance with the settlement standards agreed in the contract. This indicates that both parties recognized the choice of the Changde Arbitration Commission agreed upon to resolve their dispute over the outstanding project funds. In its appeal to the Hunan High People's Court, Changde Arts and Crafts School argued that the contract actually performed by the parties and the supplementary agreement did not contain an arbitration clause, and that the Changde Arbitration Commission's arbitration of the case was erroneous. This argument is not supported. Therefore, the determination in the Execution Ruling No. 14 (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi of Hunan High People's Court, which states that "the supplementary agreement did not stipulate a dispute resolution method, and thus the project costs for the hydropower installation and decoration works in the supplementary agreement do not fall within the scope of the arbitration agreement, and the arbitral award ruled on these project costs, exceeding the scope of arbitration," is incorrect and shall be corrected. The result of the Execution Ruling No. 8 (2012) Chang Zhi Bu Zi of Changde Intermediate People's Court is correct and shall be upheld.

In summary, pursuant to Article 20, Paragraph 2 of the Arbitration Law of the PRC and Article 129 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Execution Work of People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), the ruling is as follows:

1. Set aside the Execution Ruling No. 14 (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Zhi Jian Zi of Hunan High People's Court;

2. Uphold the Execution Ruling No. 8 (2012) Chang Zhi Bu Zi of Changde Intermediate People's Court.

This ruling shall take legal effect upon service.

Presiding Judge: He Dongning

Acting Judge: Xiang Guohui

Acting Judge: Gu Junjie

September 24, 2015

Clerk: Zhang Qiaoyun

[Brief Introduction of the Presiding Judge]

He Dongning, Senior Judge, born in 1966, holds a Master of Laws degree, and has served as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2011.
